transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-08
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~50 min
Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Dr. Nina Kumar (BlueAtlas), Alex Torres (CTO), Renee Park (FinOps)
Recording ID: fireflies-20260308-blueatlas-epdash-01

Summary: quick hands-on demo of the Console endpoint-level dashboards; focus on mapping endpoints -> routes -> per-endpoint cost decomposition, anomaly detection for bursts, and how to run a benchmark to show latency vs. cost tradeoffs. Customer wants VPC/private options and SOC2 artifacts; will share traffic sample for bench.

Topics: endpoint dashboards, per-endpoint cost decomposition, anomaly detection/alerts, hosted vs dedicated economics, VPC/KMS concerns, next steps for pilot.

[00:00] Liam: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, i'm liam from Redwood Inference, i'm the account lead. uh before we dive, quick intros?
[00:10] Nina: nina here, head of ml at blueatlas, we run a clinical AI routing layer and want tighter cost visibility at the endpoint level.
[00:16] Alex: alex, cto, interested in what level of isolation and throughput we can get.
[00:20] Renee: renee, finops, mainly want to understand per-endpoint chargebacks and anomaly alerts.
[00:26] Sofia: hey all, sofia, solutions engineer — i'll do the console walk-through and the benchmark plan.

[01:02] Sofia: okay sharing screen — this is a sandbox tenant; note the names are faked for demo. top left is the usage home, quick heatmap by traffic and cost. i'll jump into 'Endpoints' (sometimes shows as routes in other reports).
[01:20] Sofia: here we map each API endpoint — /v1/triage, /v1/summarize, etc — to a logical route. the key is the per-endpoint token breakdown and the runtime selection: hosted small model vs dedicated large model.
[01:38] Nina: nice — can we group by microservice tag? we have hundreds of endpoints across services.
[01:43] Sofia: yes you can tag endpoints, filter by service, team, and also by latency SLO buckets. when you click an endpoint you get a time series of requests, tokens, cost, and latency percentiles.

[02:05] [screen pause / cough]
[02:12] Sofia: so here's /v1/triage — top panel shows request count and avg latency, mid panel is token consumption by prompt vs completion, bottom is cost decomposition: infra (gpu time), model licensing (if applicable), and networking. note that infra cost is the bulk for long completions.
[02:35] Alex: how do you attribute infra? is it per-request or amortized by batch?
[02:40] Sofia: good question — we attribute at request-level using a combination of measured GPU time and batching heuristics, then amortize shared batch overhead across requests in that batch. it's not perfect, you might see small noise — we call that the batching delta.

[03:05] Liam: one thing to flag — customers sometimes ask about K-V cash accuracy — like the KV cache — we have a cache attribution lens that estimates cost-savings from prefix hits.
[03:16] Nina: oh, that was going to be my question — we use a lot of short context lookups, do you track prefix cache hits?
[03:22] Sofia: yes, prefix / KV cache hit rates are tracked and shown as a savings line item. sometimes the transcriber on our internal recordings says K-V cash, so ignore that.

[03:40] [05s pause]
[03:46] Sofia: switching to alerts — you can set anomaly detection on tokens per minute or token-cost rate. here's a sample we set for a 3x traffic spike detection; when triggered it creates a Slack webhook and also a ticket in JIRA.
[04:02] Renee: can alerts be scoped to a team or to a particular service account?
[04:06] Sofia: yep you scope them to tags or to single endpoints; RBAC ensures only owners get the alert.

[04:30] Alex: for private deployments, where does telemetry live? we can't send raw token payloads to hosted.
[04:36] Sofia: for Private (VPC) deployments, telemetry is exported as metadata only — token counts, latency, and anonymized metrics — you control retention and whether telemetry leaves your VPC. we also support on-prem mates that push to your internal prometheus.

[05:05] [short crosstalk]
[05:12] Sofia: now cost decomposition: see this stacked bar — red = GPU infra, yellow = queued batch overhead, green = cache savings, blue = model variant licensing. you can click 'drill into request sample' and see top 5 requests contributing to cost in the interval.
[05:34] Nina: does the console tie back to our billing exports? we want to reconcile to the monthly invoice.
[05:39] Sofia: yes we ingest your cloud billing exports and reconcile monthly; there is an export reconciliation report that highlights mismatches and probable root causes.

[06:00] [timestamping every ~30s starts becoming sparser in demo; transcribe as natural speech]
[06:12] Sofia: we'll demonstrate the bench run — we create a synthetic client that replays your recorded traffic (you provide a sanitized sample), we run three configurations: hosted small (cheaper, lower latency), hosted large (higher cost, better throughput), and dedicated with reserved GPU pool. we measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and per-1000-token cost.
[06:38] Renee: ok i will share last quarter's traffic dump — but note it has PHI, so we'll need an NDA addendum?
[06:45] Liam: understood — we'll send our standard DPA and an addendum for data handling; bench can run on sanitized, or we can run with synthetic that mirrors statistical properties.

[07:00] Alex: curious about autoscaling — does dedicated pool autoscale on pod count or GPU batch concurrency? we have strict quotas.
[07:07] Sofia: autoscale policies can be based on GPU utilization or request queues. for strict quotas you can set hard caps and also a burst window to allow temporary overcommit to a lower-priority tier.

[07:30] Sofia: back to the console — here's an example anomaly: a memex model warmed up and created a 6x increase in token cost for a particular endpoint. we show the causal chain: model rollout -> KV cache miss rate jumped -> higher tokens per request -> infra time went up. you can rollback from the console.
[07:55] Nina: that's useful — can we get automated rollback based on cost delta? say if cost > 20% we fallback to older model?
[08:02] Sofia: yes, it's configurable. you can set cost-based fallback policies; they're evaluated alongside accuracy regression checks if you push eval sets.

[08:25] [short pause, typing noise]
[08:33] Sofia: on the subject of evals, we integrate with our Optimize toolkit — when you run model comparisons we tie eval metrics to endpoints so you can see quality vs cost. example: model A saved 30% but lost 1.2% F1 on clinical NER, flagged on the eval dashboard.
[08:54] Nina: evals matter a lot for us — losing NER quality affects downstream triage. can we pin an endpoint to a specific model version per route?
[09:01] Sofia: yes pinning is supported — pin route /v1/triage to model v1.4 while others get v2.0. rollback rules apply per-pin too.

[09:20] Alex: fine-grained RBAC — can engineers see token costs? we prefer finance-only visibility for dollar amounts.
[09:27] Sofia: RBAC allows you to separate metrics: engineers can see raw metrics and percent deltas; only finance gets currency views. there's an audit log for access.

[09:45] Renee: what about encryption? we use a managed KMS and HSM for keys.
[09:50] Sofia: we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations; secrets never leave the control plane; for Private deployments you can run the control plane in your VPC. we will share the KMS playbook doc.

[10:10] [pause, someone steps away briefly]
[10:20] Sofia: quick demo of the 'Cost Explorer' — you can break down spend by endpoint, by team, by model, and by time window; apply smoothing and choose attribution method (per-request or per-token).
[10:40] Liam: many customers run a hybrid: route cheap quantized model for low-risk paths and route high-precision to dedicated GPUs for critical paths. costs align well.

[11:00] Nina: question: we use an LLM for redaction before triage — does that show up as a separate upstream cost?
[11:06] Sofia: yes — you can create multi-step pipelines in the console; each step has its own cost line, and we show end-to-end cost per user request.

[11:30] [Sofia points to a 'Top Contributors' table]
[11:35] Sofia: this table lists endpoints that drive 80/20 of cost; clicking a row shows sample requests and the exact token lengths. you can export this as CSV for chargeback.
[11:48] Renee: export useful — can format to our internal chargeback CSV schema?
[11:52] Sofia: yes templates can be applied or you can map columns.

[12:10] Alex: for the bench, what are expected savings? ballpark.
[12:14] Sofia: varies, but we've seen 20-60% unit-cost reductions with caching + quantization + routing. dedicated is often higher throughput with lower per-token cost at scale but needs commit. we'll show numbers after the bench.

[12:32] [brief laugh]
[12:36] Nina: any limitations? we have some long-running streaming calls, will that break the attribution model?
[12:42] Sofia: streaming is supported; attribution measures GPU time per stream and accounts for idle time vs token generation. edge cases require calibration; we'll note that on the bench plan.

[13:00] [speaker labeled "Speaker 1" — transcription artefact]
[13:03] Speaker 1: (muffled) what's the SLA on dedicated clusters?
[13:07] Liam: SLA varies by contract tier; standard dedicated has 99.9 uptime SLA, enterprise can be higher. we'll include SLA sheet.

[13:30] Sofia: last piece — scheduled reports and anomaly runbooks. you can create a weekly 'top cost movers' email to stakeholders and a runbook for investigating large deltas, with pre-populated queries.
[13:48] Nina: that's actually what we need — runbook + alerts so ops doesn't get paged for normal churn.

[14:10] [wrap-up, next steps]
[14:15] Liam: recap — we'll provision trial tenant, sofia will run bench with the sample (or synthetic) traffic, we'll send SOC2 and network diagram, renee will share billing export. follow-up next week.
[14:30] Alex: sounds good, we'll get docs to you.
[14:34] Renee: one ask — can you include a sample chargeback csv mapping for our finance team?
[14:38] Liam: yes — i'll include a template and examples.

[14:50] Sofia: links mentioned: demo deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/ep-dashboard-demo), bench playbook (https://redwood.ai/bench-playbook), SOC2 packet will be emailed.

[15:00] Meeting end.
